studies.label: Within-person laboratory experiment: personalized versus standard GAI on the Product Improvement Task

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 376), Abstract; PDF p. 4 (printed p. 379), Sect. 3.1. Random assignment is established in the related c246 report, PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Fig. 3; its final sample size is stated in PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), Participants. See notes for source linkage.
counts_source.quote: Each of the 62 students engaged in two creativity tasks: one with standard GAI (ChatGPT-4) providing generic feedback, and the other with a personalized GAI tutor (Mr. Ranedeer)

arms.name: Personalized GAI (Mr. Ranedeer)
arms.description: Each participant completed one task with Mr. Ranedeer, a personalized GPT-4 tutor in the OpenAI web interface. Students configured learning preferences and a learning plan, received Socratic-style questions, and obtained goal-aligned feedback and suggestions for refining and elaborating solutions (PDF p. 5, printed p. 380, Sect. 3.2.1 and Fig. 1).

arms.name: Standard GAI (ChatGPT-4)
arms.description: Each participant completed one task with standard ChatGPT-4 in the OpenAI web interface. It offered broad suggestions in response to queries and generated solutions on further request, supporting open-ended exploration with minimal structure (PDF p. 5, printed p. 380, Sect. 3.2.1 and Fig. 1).

studies.task: Individually propose three original and useful product-improvement solutions for each of two everyday products, a stuffed bunny and a portable coffee machine, using the assigned AI tool (PDF pp. 6-7, printed pp. 381-382, Sect. 3.4.1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4 and Mr. Ranedeer, both built on OpenAI’s GPT-4 model
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 380), Sect. 3.2.1 and Fig. 1; the model release year is not stated.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two trained raters, blind to condition, rated solutions presented in randomized order on a five-point Likert scale from worst to best. Final scores averaged the two raters. Quality is the extent to which a solution addresses the task objective. The paper does not establish domain-expert status or explain aggregation across a participant’s solutions (PDF p. 7, printed p. 382, Sect. 3.4.1).

sources.quote: quality (M = 3.50, SD = 1.00) than in the standard condition (M = 3.08, SD = 1.12; p = .001; r = .42).
Each of the 62 students engaged in two creativity tasks: one with standard GAI (ChatGPT-4) providing generic feedback, and the other with a personalized GAI tutor (Mr. Ranedeer)
Differences between conditions were examined using Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests

estimates.notes: The paper names Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests but prints no W or Z statistic, degrees of freedom, contrast SE, or confidence interval for this outcome. No difference, standardized mean effect, or paired SE has been computed. The reported r is retained with its printed positive sign; its standardizer is not defined. The same participants received both conditions, so arm counts repeat the study sample and n_total counts each person once. Counts come from the statement that every student completed both tasks; the results do not repeat an outcome-specific n or report exclusions. The analysis is coded as participant-level following the within-student design, but neither report explains how the three solutions per task were combined; sd_level is therefore null and se_basis is not_reported. Fig. 4A (PDF p. 9, printed p. 384) repeats the outcomes graphically; no values were estimated from its bars. Related c246 Table 2 reports different r values despite matching means, SDs and p-values; those values are not substituted here.

open_items: Neither report explains how the three solutions per participant per condition were aggregated. The unit underlying the printed SDs and the participant basis of the paired precision therefore remain unconfirmed; sd_level is null.

c041 reports no numeric Wilcoxon test statistic, paired-difference SD, within-person covariance, contrast SE, or CI for the creativity outcomes. It also does not state the formula or standardizer for r. Participant-level paired precision cannot be confirmed from the printed chapter.
The paired-condition results are reported without separate first-round statistics. No first_round estimate can be transcribed from this chapter.

The chapter states that each participant completed both tasks but gives no outcome-specific analysis counts, missing-data accounting, or number of nonzero pairs used in the signed-rank tests. Estimate counts retain the printed complete study sample.

c246 Table 2 (PDF p. 11, printed p. 175) has identical creativity means, SDs and p-values but different signed effect sizes, and supplies additional test statistics and effect-size intervals. Neither report explicitly explains or corrects the discrepancy; retain source-specific values and resolve the effect-size definitions before using them for paired precision.
The GPT-4 model release year is not stated in the chapter or related report and remains null.
notes: Extraction B, 2026-10-09. The complete c041 markdown conversion was read, including references, and its PDF figures and tables were checked first; every numeric estimate was checked against PDF p. 8. The chapter contains no appendix or identified supplement, preregistration, data repository, or primary outcome designation. Its entire eligible statistic inventory is the two arm means and SDs, p-value, and reported r for each of quality, elaboration and originality, all retained above. Measurement reliability is additionally reported on PDF p. 7 (printed p. 382), Sect. 3.4.1: “inter-rater reliability was high (Cronbach’s α = 0.88, 0.90, 0.86, respectively)”, in quality, elaboration, originality order. These are rating-reliability statistics, not treatment effects. The full c246 markdown, including its embedded appendix, was also read because the reconciled screening form uses that separate report to establish randomization and sample overlap. Its PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Fig. 3 was visually checked and explicitly states “Random assignment of feedback sequence”. The chapter itself states only counterbalancing (PDF p. 6, printed p. 381, Sect. 3.3). The lab_rct classification and randomized counts rely on the inferred shared-sample link, not on a randomization statement in c041. Country is supported by c246 PDF p. 4 (printed p. 168), Participants: “A total of 62 Chinese university students (41 female) from a normal university participated in the study.” c246 PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Procedure, and p. 9, Fig. 3 clarify that the product order is the same in both sequences while AI order reverses. Its Appendix, PDF pp. 20-21 (printed pp. 184-185), contains intervention settings and examples, not further creativity contrasts. c246 is a separate report, not a supplement to c041; none of its outcome estimates or test values have been imported. Local related-report PDF: C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Chen et al (2026) - Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback.pdf. Repeated arm Ns describe the same people in a crossover and must not be added. No statistics were derived or read numerically from graph heights; source quotes preserve printed precision. The schema unit follows the within-student comparison while the unreported aggregation level is left unresolved for standardization and pooling.
